record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Can primordial Big Bang nucleosynthesis be tested without circularly choosing inferred primordial abundances and adjustable parameters, and can it consistently account for low reported helium mass fractions, uncertain deuterium evolution and production mechanisms, excessive beryllium abundances, baryon-density requirements, and the preference in some fits for two rather than three neutrino species?

evidence.quote: However, galaxies of poor metal content, implying minimal stellar contamination, show the mass fraction of 4He as low as 0.21 [172]. Even allowing for error bars this is far too low to match the Big Bang predictions.
The Deuterium evolution and mechanisms of possible Deuterium production from the Big Bang until now are still not properly understood[174, 175].

Perhaps the most important aspect to criticize is the methodology itself to test the primordial nucleosynthesis[182]: Instead of trying to make predictions that can be tested by observation, cosmologists take observations that can be made, such as measurements of the abundances in Population II material, and try to determine the primordial abundances, knowing a priori what answer is needed to fit some particular model.
Still, as we see, some open questions are discussed in the model and whether this can be substituted by alternative models remains to be seen.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Standard Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) predicts the primordial mass/number abundances of the light elements ⁴He, D, ³He, ⁷Li and ⁹Be as functions of the baryon-to-photon ratio η (equivalently the baryon density parameter Ω_b h²) and the effective number of light neutrino species N_ν, given the standard set of nuclear reaction rates and a Friedmann–Lemaître background.

Address the following methodological and empirical questions about this framework:

1. Can the predictions of standard BBN be confronted with observation in a non-circular way — that is, by genuine a priori predictions of light-element abundances that are tested against measurements, rather than by inferring "primordial" abundances from Population II (and similar) data under the assumption of the model whose parameters are simultaneously being adjusted?

2. Within a single choice of η (consistent with the baryon density determined independently, e.g. from the cosmic microwave background) and a fixed N_ν, can standard BBN simultaneously be made consistent with:
   (a) reports of a ⁴He mass fraction Y_p as low as ≈ 0.21 in very metal-poor galaxies,
   (b) the observed scatter and poorly-understood galactic chemical evolution and possible non-primordial production mechanisms of deuterium,
   (c) observed beryllium (⁹Be) abundances in metal-poor halo stars that appear in excess of standard predictions,
   (d) the baryon density required by CMB and large-scale structure data, and
   (e) the apparent preference of some abundance fits for N_ν ≈ 2 rather than the Standard Model value N_ν = 3?

Either exhibit a single consistent choice of parameters and astrophysical assumptions that reconciles (a)–(e), or prove that no such reconciliation is possible within standard BBN, identifying which item provides the obstruction.
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2025, standard BBN predictions for D and ⁴He show excellent agreement with high-precision observations and with the baryon density inferred from the CMB; N_ν = 3 is consistent with current data. The historical concerns about very low Y_p ≈ 0.21 have largely been retracted as observational systematics improved. The lithium-7 problem (and a milder deuterium-lithium tension) remains unresolved, with proposed astrophysical (stellar depletion, mixing) and exotic-physics solutions still under active investigation. Thus the methodological/empirical bundle is partially resolved: most items are settled in favor of standard BBN, while ⁷Li (and the methodological circularity concern in a strict sense) remain open.

status_evidence.title: The cosmological lithium problem (A&A 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: The discrepancy between predictions of primordial nucleosynthesis and observed lithium abundance in Spite plateau stars remains, attributed either to challenges to standard nucleosynthesis or to post-formation stellar processes.

status_evidence.title: Precision big bang nucleosynthesis with improved Helium-4 predictions
status_evidence.snippet: BBN and CMB predictions show excellent agreement with high-redshift observational data for D and 4He; Y_p = 0.24709±0.00017.
status_evidence.claim: D and ⁴He are consistent with standard BBN at the percent level, with N_ν=3.

status_evidence.title: The Deuterium-Lithium tension in BBN — Triton Station (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: A residual tension between deuterium and lithium constraints in BBN persists.
status_evidence.claim: A deuterium-lithium tension remains under active discussion.
